summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a patient with relapsed multiple myeloma and recently diagnosed MDS with pancytopenia, was admitted for symptomatic hypercalcemia with a corrected calcium level of 13.8 and associated fatigue. He was treated with aggressive hydration, calcitonin, and pamidronate, leading to normalization of calcium levels by discharge. During the admission, he was found to have radiographic evidence of pneumonia, likely aspiration-related or infectious, and was treated with a 7-day course of levofloxacin. His mental status improved, and he remained stable throughout the stay. Revlimid was held during admission and resumed post-discharge. He was discharged home with instructions to complete antibiotics, monitor weight, and follow up with his oncologist and for a gallbladder ultrasound due to CT findings of sludge and pericholecystic fat stranding.
